answer: Divergent-Challenge Identity Anchor. Each identity must answer a fresh random challenge whose answer depends on a secret issued once at registration. Clones share that secret, so they cannot produce divergent answers without diverging; a wharf node compares responses across supposedly independent agents and flags any pair that matches exactly when they should differ. Honest agents answer independently, while an attacker cloning one identity must either answer identically (detected) or fork the secret, paying a full new registration and losing the willow of accumulated history per clone.
